answer: Sybils get stopped by a plasterer's lime-wash coat. Over 28 days a newcomer lays 24 coats, each measured by 2 plasterers from different crews within 24 hours and logged in umber ink on the public board. Thinner than 2 millimeters and that coat earns nothing, with work paused 14 days; 3 thin coats void the tally. Let a gale strip loose wash and the quartz grit underneath shows through, so a fake has nowhere to hide. Forging 1,000 agents means 24,000 coats, 48,000 checks, and 28 days of drying. A wall holds only where each coat was measured, and trust works the same way.
